data.title: Traditional Media Used to Launder the Claim
data.summary:
The campaign secured coverage in established outlets, after which the claim could be
cited to a credible source rather than to its origin.
data.description:
Laundering through legitimate media is the highest-value move available to an operation.
Once an outlet has reported that a claim is circulating, the claim acquires a citable
source, and subsequent amplification points at the outlet rather than at the accounts
that manufactured it.

The usual route is a journalist acting in good faith on what appears to be genuine public
concern. The volume manufactured earlier in the campaign is what makes the story real:
the coverage is accurate — people are saying this — and accurate coverage of manufactured
activity still completes the laundering.

For the report, distinguish the outlet's conduct from the operation's. Treating a
journalist as part of the campaign is both usually wrong and certain to destroy the
client's ability to correct the record.
data.recommendation:
* Approach the outlet with the coordination evidence rather than with a complaint about
  the coverage; most will report the coordination if it is evidenced.
* Prioritise correcting the laundered citation, since downstream amplification points at
  it rather than at the original content.
* Maintain the distinction in all communications between the outlet and the operation.
data.short_recommendation: Take the coordination evidence to the outlet; correct the citation.
